item.company: George Mason University – Enterprise Risk Management
item.title: Policy and Risk Specialist
item.description:
This position is open until filled and applications may be reviewed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 10/9/2026.

Note: The original priority deadline of May 8, 2026 has passed, but the position remains open until filled. No visa sponsorship. Hybrid eligible in Fairfax, VA. Three professional references, cover letter, and resume required. Apply at jobs.gmu.edu (search Policy and Risk Specialist).

George Mason University’s Enterprise Risk Management (ERM) unit promotes institutional resilience by identifying, assessing, and managing risks that could affect the university’s mission. The unit also oversees policy management and building code compliance to ensure clear, consistent, and accountable governance across the institution. The Policy and Risk Specialist strengthens organizational effectiveness by coordinating the development, review, and maintenance of institutional policies while supporting the identification, assessment, and mitigation of enterprise-level risks. 3–5 years of experience required. Salary commensurate with education and experience (Pay Band 04). Fairfax, VA (hybrid eligible).

Key responsibilities include (Policy Development, Management & Governance Support): serving as University Policy Manager coordinating the full lifecycle of institutional policies including drafting, review, approval, publishing, and archiving; guiding policy owners through required processes, templates, timelines, and governance structures; maintaining the policy repository and ensuring version control, consistency, and clarity in policy language; and supporting transparency by keeping the policy website up-to-date. (ERM Support): preparing draft materials for meetings and presentations focused on ERM; coordinating AV support and taking meeting notes and preparing minutes; serving as project manager tracking and coordinating requests and follow-up with Executive Risk Owners and Action Plan Risk Owners; and utilizing technology in support of the ERM program including inputting data, preparing reports, and utilizing analysis capabilities. (Administrative, Data, and Reporting Support): scheduling complex meetings including Policy Management Group meetings, ERM Council meetings, and meetings with senior leadership; maintaining accurate documentation, meeting minutes, schedules, and tracking systems; supporting the preparation of reports for senior leadership, auditors, and governance bodies; and assisting with data management, analysis, and process-improvement.

Qualifications: a bachelor’s degree in a related field (master’s preferred); 3–5 years of professional experience in policy development, risk management, compliance, project management, governance, or a related administrative or analytical role (5–7 years preferred); experience supporting complex processes involving multiple stakeholders; experience preparing reports, documentation, or communication for leadership or governance bodies; knowledge of Microsoft Suite (SharePoint, Teams, Word, Excel, PowerPoint), DocuSign, and Adobe Suite; and strong written communication and project management skills. No visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary commensurate with education and experience (Pay Band 04). Comprehensive GMU benefits. Hybrid eligible in Fairfax, VA. Three professional references, cover letter, and resume required. Apply at jobs.gmu.edu.

item.title: Risk Assessment Program Analyst
item.description:
⚠️ APPLICATION DEADLINE: September 27, 2026 at 11:55 PM EDT — apply immediately. Applications accepted online only via the Virginia State Job website.

Note: This is a restricted position (funding dependent). A 1-year probationary period is required of all newly hired Commonwealth of Virginia employees. Essential personnel designation — may be required to work during emergencies including inclement weather and natural or human-caused disasters, which may require irregular hours and work at locations other than the official duty station. No visa sponsorship. E-Verify. Salary is negotiable up to 8,000; offers will not be made outside the hiring range.

The Virginia Department of Emergency Management (VDEM) seeks a Risk Assessment Program Analyst to serve as the lead coordinator for state-level risk and capability assessments that evaluate the threats, hazards, vulnerabilities, and capabilities of the Commonwealth to inform pre-disaster planning, preparedness, and hazard mitigation strategies. The position is responsible for two federally mandated assessments: the Threat and Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (THIRA) and Stakeholder Preparedness Review (SPR), and the State Hazard Mitigation Plan’s Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA). North Chesterfield, VA (Richmond area). Salary 5,000–8,000.

Key responsibilities include: ensuring the successful completion of the federally mandated THIRA and SPR by leading the collaborative effort to identify risks of greatest concern to the Commonwealth, facilitating conversations that determine the capabilities needed to address those risks, identifying current preparedness levels, and evaluating capability gaps; leading the collection and integration of qualitative and quantitative data from diverse stakeholders into clear findings that inform the THIRA and SPR; supporting the systematic identification and description of hazards affecting the Commonwealth for the State Hazard Mitigation Plan’s HIRA, including analysis of hazard probability, location, intensity, and impacts; identifying and representing the vulnerability of state assets; and synthesizing qualitative and quantitative data into actionable findings that directly inform hazard mitigation priorities and strategies.

Qualifications: demonstrated experience interpreting and applying federal emergency management policy and doctrine, including FEMA’s Comprehensive Preparedness Guide (CPG) 101, CPG 201, and FEMA hazard mitigation planning policy; demonstrated ability to analyze and synthesize qualitative and quantitative data; exceptional interpersonal, written, and verbal communication skills; demonstrated ability to facilitate stakeholder meetings and present complex findings to non-technical audiences; proven experience in project management including developing timelines, milestones, status reports, and executive briefings; and experience conducting gap analyses, THIRA, HIRA, and similar evaluations. Experience in local, regional, or state government emergency management, homeland security, planning, or resilience preferred. Must be legally authorized to work in the U.S.; no visa sponsorship.

Compensation and logistics: salary 5,000–8,000. Comprehensive Virginia state benefits. North Chesterfield, VA (Richmond area). Restricted position (funding dependent). Essential personnel designation. 1-year probationary period. Deadline: September 27, 2026 at 11:55 PM EDT — apply only via Virginia State Job website.

Compensation and logistics: salary 6,000–4,000. Comprehensive Guidehouse benefits including medical, dental, vision, 401(k), parental leave, tuition reimbursement, student loan paydown, and mobility stipend. Arlington, VA. Up to 25% travel. Campus 2027 hire (graduate by Summer 2027).

item.description:

Note: White & Case recruits for legal assistant positions throughout the year, targeting entry-level candidates primarily in early winter and spring. A four-year college degree with a minimum GPA of 3.5 is required, along with relevant work experience. Apply via whitecase.com. White & Case is a leading global law firm, among the first U.S.-based firms to establish a truly global presence, providing counsel and representation in virtually every area of law that affects cross-border business. Legal assistants at White & Case are smart, motivated, and dynamic members of collaborative teams across a variety of practice groups. Four types of legal assistant positions are available: Corporate, Litigation, Evening, and Senior legal assistants.

Key responsibilities include: multitasking in a fast-paced environment; working effectively with others across partners, associates, and staff; exercising good judgment and maintaining high ethical standards; and providing practice-specific legal support. Foreign language skills are often needed for certain client matters. White & Case offers structured training sessions, an open-door culture, and mentoring to support professional development.

Qualifications: a four-year college degree required; minimum GPA of 3.5; relevant work experience required; foreign language skills a plus for certain client matters; ability to multitask in a fast-paced environment; ability to work effectively with others; and demonstrated good judgment and high ethical standards.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (competitive for a top global law firm; confirm via application). Comprehensive White & Case benefits. New York, NY. Rolling recruitment; early winter and spring are peak hiring periods. Apply via whitecase.com. Questions: contact Jonathan (Jack) Klaren at jklaren@whitecase.com.

item.title: Associate Policy Analyst, Global Program
item.description:
Application deadline: September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET. Apply by submitting a cover letter, resume, and a 1,000-word writing sample on an immigration policy of your choosing to hr@migrationpolicy.org. Label each file with your last name. Use 'Associate Policy Analyst - Global Program' as the subject line and include how you heard about the position. AI tools may be used in the writing sample but must be disclosed. No phone calls or emails to MPI staff. Only candidates being considered will be contacted.

The Migration Policy Institute (MPI) is an independent, nonpartisan, evidence-informed think tank focused on the movement of people worldwide. The Global Program acts as a policy laboratory for innovative, evidence-based, and politically feasible solutions to migration policy challenges, with an established portfolio of projects in Latin America, East Africa, and Europe, and emerging work in South/Southeast Asia, the Middle East and North Africa, and Australia. The Associate Policy Analyst will support the team with rigorous empirical research and comparative analysis on a range of migration policy topics. This position offers direct exposure to MPI's behind-the-scenes policy advising and convening. The role is based in Washington, DC; remote work worldwide will be considered for the right candidate. Master's degree + 3-5 years required. Salary $62,000-$67,000 (U.S.-based).

Key responsibilities include: delivering in-depth policy analysis with clear interpretations and actionable recommendations, and helping shape the methodology behind new research projects; drafting and editing background notes, analytical reports, policy briefs, and other research materials with minimal supervision and under tight deadlines; contributing to and co-authoring MPI publications and short-form work, with opportunities to single- or lead-author policy briefs as experience grows; assisting senior staff in fundraising and grant management duties including contributing to grant proposals and reports; supporting the organization of high-level roundtables and private meetings including developing agendas and concept notes, liaising with participants, and briefing speakers; and, in time, engaging with the news media.

Qualifications: a master's degree with 3-5 years of direct experience, or equivalent combination; strong research and analytical skills with the ability to collect and make sense of large volumes of data from primary and secondary sources; knowledge of international migration trends and policies with specific expertise in one or more countries outside the United States preferred (particularly in Africa, Latin America, or Europe); sharp writing and oral communication skills; and high motivation with the ability to juggle multiple assignments in a fast-paced environment. Experience conducting original quantitative analysis using statistical programming software is a plus.

Compensation and logistics: salary $62,000-$67,000 (U.S.-based; remote worldwide compensation reviewed based on candidate's location and local regulations). Generous MPI benefits package. Washington, DC (remote worldwide considered). Deadline: September 30, 2026 at 5:00 PM ET.

item.title: Sr. Policy Analyst
item.description:
Application review begins October 11, 2026 and will continue on a rolling basis thereafter.

Voices for Virginia's Children is hiring a Sr. Policy Analyst to drive statewide, systems-level change with a focus on Early Childhood Care & Education and Maternal Health policy. The Sr. Policy Analyst will analyze policy and data, develop and advance legislative and administrative solutions, build relationships with policymakers and partners, and help translate complex policy issues into actionable strategies for change. This role requires a minimum of 3 years of experience in state-level policy advocacy. The position is hybrid in Richmond, VA (Wednesdays in-office required; additional in-person days required during the Virginia General Assembly session). Salary $68,000-$74,000.

Key responsibilities include (Policy Advocacy and Leadership): leading Voices' policy work in early childhood care and education and maternal health; working collaboratively with policy and engagement staff to create and advance a multi-disciplinary policy agenda for infants, young children, and families; monitoring legislative and administrative developments; analyzing policy and research; identifying opportunities for systems change; developing evidence-based policy recommendations; providing policy analysis support to internal and external partners; and having primary responsibility for advancing these issue areas during Virginia's General Assembly session. (Community Relationship Building): leading and participating in various coalitions within the focus area; serving as the main Voices liaison for partner organizations; providing support and technical assistance to partner coalitions and state workgroups; and working in partnership with the Director of Engagement and Virginia's Youth in Action (VAYA) members to ensure that youth voice and lived expertise are centered in policy recommendations. (Strategic Communications): working with the Communications Manager on developing and executing communications including policy briefs, one-pagers, blogs, and other advocacy materials; and conducting and participating in trainings and presentations. (Racial Equity): promoting racial equity across all dimensions of work, ensuring that policies put forward are assessed for their impact on all races.

Qualifications: strong verbal and written communication skills; a minimum of 3 years of experience working in state-level policy advocacy with knowledge of the Virginia state legislative process and evidence-based policymaking; ability to build relationships with legislators, community members, partner organizations, and other stakeholders; ability to effectively analyze data and research to identify trends and inform policymaking; and strong commitment to social, economic, and racial justice with active centering of equity and inclusion. Candidates should bring substantive knowledge in at least one of early childhood care and education or maternal health and demonstrate the ability to quickly develop expertise across both areas.

Compensation and logistics: salary $68,000-$74,000 (to preserve opportunity for salary growth, Voices typically does not hire above the mid-range). Benefits include fully covered health, dental, and vision employee premiums, health and dependent care FSAs, 30 days of PTO and 12 paid holidays, paid parental leave, a retirement plan with 3% employer contribution (no required employee match), professional development stipend, and monthly remote work stipend. Hybrid in Richmond, VA (Wednesdays in-office required; additional in-person during GA session). Application review begins October 11, 2026.

item.title: Youth Development Specialist – El Salvador
item.description:
This position was posted with no close date and applications may be reviewed or closed on a rolling basis — interested applicants should apply ASAP! The posting will be removed from Batten Connect on 9/29/2026.

Note: Peace Corps Volunteers receive a living stipend, not a salary. This is a two-year volunteer commitment requiring U.S. citizenship. Volunteers live and work in host communities, receiving a stipend and other support including housing, medical care, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service.

The Peace Corps is seeking U.S. citizens to serve as Youth Development Specialists in El Salvador. Youth make up more than a quarter of El Salvador's population, yet many young people face social and economic challenges including economic hardship, low school completion rates, limited life skills development opportunities, and barriers to civic engagement. Only half of youth complete lower secondary school and even fewer complete upper secondary school. As a Youth Development Specialist, you will collaborate with school staff to equip youth with essential life skills such as communication, empathy, creative problem-solving, and goal setting, working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments that encourage youth participation in community projects and civic engagement.

Key responsibilities include: collaborating with school staff to teach essential life skills to youth; working alongside community leaders to create supportive environments for youth participation; contributing to community projects and civic engagement initiatives; building relationships with host community members; and exchanging knowledge and helping transform lives for future generations.

Qualifications: U.S. citizenship required; bachelor's degree (typical requirement for Peace Corps service); demonstrated commitment to community development, education, or youth work. Visit the Peace Corps El Salvador project page for full details and application information.

Compensation and logistics: living stipend provided (not a salary); additional benefits include housing support, medical and dental care, language and cultural training, and a readjustment allowance upon completion of service. El Salvador. 2-year commitment. U.S. citizenship required.

Compensation and logistics: salary not stated (federal NAF pay scale). NAF benefits package. Multiple Navy installation locations. Official transcripts required at time of application.
